note: Tests that fail on the Linux runner for reasons that do not exist on this Mac. The Mac allowlist (unit-known-red.json) does NOT transfer: it names this machine's environment, and the nightly runs ubuntu-24.04-arm. An entry here is a claim with evidence, not a mute button — check it with `node local/check-nightly-linux-parity.mjs --failures <downloaded-artifacts>`, which fails on any red that is not listed and reports a listed test that passed as prunable.

entries.test: serializes concurrent keepHistory and disconnectOnly checkpoints
entries.evidence: Failed on Linux three times: run 40485647652 (scheduled, nplez1/main @7c53c12a17) and run 40517494613 (dispatch, nplez1/main @ddc2a7827f), both with DaemonConnectionLostError: Disconnected out of disconnectOnly() at the test's own line 292, and again in run 40675428994 (scheduled 2026-10-28, nplez1/main @7b86cb08), where local/check-unit-shard-verdict.mjs absorbed it as an already-triaged red. Passed in every run since: 40695078222 (dispatch, nplez1/main @d96a57ffc6 — shard 3 green; that run failed only shard 1's cooldown assertion), 40701735011 (dispatch, nplez1/main @1776dcc575, all five shards) and 40797794635 (dispatch, nplez1/main @fdd5850d0f, all five shards), the last two also reporting it as a prunable entry. It is intermittent rather than deterministic — earlier pass: 40540799557 on branch nplez1/Fork-Opt-P2 @e2f7f28789. Passes 3/3 on this Mac too, so it is not a Mac allowlist entry either. Every file in the stack is upstream-owned with zero fork hunks: daemon-pty-event-subscriptions.ts, daemon/client.ts, daemon-client-pending-requests.ts, daemon-pty-adapter.ts and the test itself. Not fixable inside the fork without divergence, which costs more at the next sync than the red costs now.
entries.exit: Remove when upstream serialises finishDisconnectOnly against in-flight requests, or when this test passes on Linux in five consecutive scheduled nights. Two would be too weak on this history: three failures in seven observations make a chance double-pass about 1 in 3 with nothing fixed, and every pass so far is a dispatch. Seen so far, in order: failed(scheduled), failed(dispatch), passed(dispatch), failed(scheduled), passed(dispatch), passed(dispatch), passed(dispatch).
